description: Two synthetic, non-client profiles for transparent research screening. Candidate lists are illustrative and do not establish legal applicability, national implementation, or legal advice.

profiles.name: Irish payment institution (illustrative)
assumedActivities: Reliance on ICT and service providers
profiles.note: Illustrative assumptions only. Actual permissions, group exemptions, size, services, outsourcing and Irish implementing rules require individual verification.

candidates.why: ICT operational-resilience and third-party arrangements warrant review for financial entities.
candidates.verify: Confirm licensing category, applicable DORA perimeter, service providers and exemptions.

candidates.why: Payment and staff data processing creates questions about data protection roles and safeguards.
candidates.verify: Map personal data, controller/processor roles and lawful processing grounds.

candidates.why: Cybersecurity rules and Irish transposition may create questions depending on entity classification and sector.
candidates.verify: Check the current Irish implementing law, sector coverage, size and any DORA overlap before treating it as an obligation.

candidates.why: Some payment providers use fraud or customer-support AI; the EU AI Act may be worth screening if such systems are used.
candidates.verify: Determine whether AI systems are used and the actual operator roles and covered use categories.

profiles.name: EU AI-enabled SaaS provider (illustrative)
profiles.note: Illustrative assumptions only. Classification as an AI-system provider, cloud service or digital product depends on the actual product and legal definitions.

candidates.why: Potential AI-related provider or deployer roles require an initial legal classification.
candidates.verify: Identify the systems, actors, risk classes and applicable provisions and dates.

candidates.why: Amendments to AI Act timing may affect planning where the underlying AI Act applies.
candidates.verify: Check original provisions, subsequent amendments and current application dates.

candidates.why: SaaS processing of customer or staff data merits a controller/processor and data-flow assessment.
candidates.verify: Identify processing activities, roles, legal bases, transfer arrangements and contracts.

candidates.why: The EU Cyber Resilience Act may warrant screening for certain products with digital elements.
candidates.verify: Determine whether the specific software/product model falls within product scope and its phased obligations.

candidates.why: Cloud service and data access rules may matter for some covered services or product relationships.
candidates.verify: Identify the type of cloud/data processing service and whether specific chapters are relevant.

candidates.why: Digital Services Act questions arise only for particular intermediary or platform functions.
candidates.verify: Check whether the service actually falls within DSA intermediary-service definitions.
